subChunks.title: Accessibility with Tailwind
subChunks.hookHtml: Accessibility is not optional — it is a legal requirement under WCAG, the ADA, and the European Accessibility Act, and it is a professional expectation at every serious company. Tailwind gives you all the tools. Using them correctly is the mark of an expert.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Lyra the Scribe: "A spell that works only for some readers is a spell half-cast. Let me show you the five habits that cover ninety percent of accessibility work in a Tailwind codebase."

Habit 1: focus-visible: over focus:

// ❌ WRONG — shows a ring on every mouse click (annoying)
<button class="focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500">Save</button>

// ✅ CORRECT — ring appears only when focused via keyboard
<button class="focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500 focus-visible:ring-offset-2">Save</button>

focus-visible: maps to :focus-visible — the browser only applies this when focus came from the keyboard, not a mouse click. Removing the outline entirely is a WCAG violation.

Habit 2: sr-only for icon-only controls

<button class="p-2 rounded-md focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" class="w-5 h-5" />
  <span class="sr-only">Close dialog</span>
</button>

Always mark SVG icons with aria-hidden="true" to prevent them being read aloud as noise.

Habit 3: ARIA state variants

<!-- Chevron that rotates when dropdown opens -->
<button aria-expanded="false" class="flex items-center gap-2">
  Menu
  <svg class="w-4 h-4 transition-transform aria-expanded:rotate-180" />
</button>

<!-- Tab active state -->
<button role="tab" aria-selected="false"
  class="px-4 py-2 text-sm border-b-2 border-transparent
         aria-selected:border-blue-600 aria-selected:text-blue-600">
  Overview
</button>

Habit 4: Colour contrast

WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal body text and 3:1 for large text. Several popular combinations fail:

// Contrast ratios against white background:
gray-400:  3.5:1  ❌ fails for body text
gray-500:  4.6:1  ✓ barely passes — prefer gray-600
gray-600:  5.9:1  ✓ solid
blue-400:  2.5:1  ❌ use blue-700 (5.5:1) for text on white

Habit 5: Reduced motion

<div class="animate-bounce motion-reduce:animate-none">
<div class="transition-transform duration-300 motion-reduce:transition-none">

Add motion-reduce: to every animated element. Users with vestibular disorders can be physically harmed by excessive motion.

Lyra: "Five habits. Write them on the wall above your desk. Every component you ship should pass all five before it leaves your branch."

storyBeats.text: A blindfolded figure sits at a desk in the lamp-lit room below the library, tracing a page with her fingertips. Lyra speaks quietly beside you.

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: focus-visible: instead of focus:. sr-only on every icon-only button. ARIA state variants. Contrast ratios above 4.5:1. motion-reduce: on every animation. Five habits. All five. Every component.

subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode: Please enter a valid email.
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build an accessible navigation menu from scratch. It must include: a skip-to-content link (sr-only focus:not-sr-only), keyboard-focusable nav links with focus-visible:ring-2, and at least one aria-current="page" active state style.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain to a junior developer why removing outline: none from a button is a WCAG violation, but using focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 is acceptable. What is the practical difference?

options: Visually hides content while keeping it accessible to screen readers
Removes content from the DOM and the accessibility tree
Hides content from screen readers but keeps it visually visible
Sets display: none on the element
questions.answer: Visually hides content while keeping it accessible to screen readers
questions.explanation: sr-only uses position, size, clipping, and overflow CSS to make an element invisible on screen while keeping it in the accessibility tree, where screen readers can still announce it.

questions.prompt: A dropdown button toggles aria-expanded between true and false in JavaScript. Which Tailwind approach correctly rotates a chevron icon when the dropdown is open?
options: class="transition-transform aria-expanded:rotate-180" on the chevron SVG
class="rotate-180" toggled by JavaScript alongside aria-expanded
class="open:rotate-180" which fires on the open state
questions.answer: class="transition-transform aria-expanded:rotate-180" on the chevron SVG
questions.explanation: Tailwind's aria-expanded: variant applies when the element (or its closest ARIA-attributable ancestor) has aria-expanded="true". This keeps JS responsible for ARIA, and CSS responds declaratively.

questions.prompt: What is the WCAG AA minimum contrast ratio for normal body text?
questions.explanation: WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold). WCAG AAA raises these to 7:1 and 4.5:1 respectively. gray-400 on white (3.5:1) fails for body text — use gray-600 (5.9:1) or darker.
